article.abstract: Lanthanide-chelating lipids offer a route to responsive soft submicron lipid-particle materials, yet how their interfacial properties encode membrane curvature and temperature-dependent optical behavior remain poorly understood. Here, polymer-free monoolein/DOPC submicron lipid particles doped with Eu-DTPA-PE, with the monoolein : (DOPC + Eu-DTPA-PE) molar ratio fixed at 17 : 3, over Eu loadings of 1-12.5 mol% are examined using temperature-dependent polarized light microscopy (PLM), dynamic light scattering (DLS), and Eu 3+ fluorescence to relate interfacial structure to curvature-linked changes in mesoscopic organization. In the absence of chelating lipids, MO/DOPC submicron lipid particles display an isotropic optical response at low temperature that reproducibly develops strong birefringence upon heating, behavior consistent with but not uniquely diagnostic of a transition from a cubic-like to a more anisotropic nonlamellar state. Introducing low Eu-DTPA levels (1-2.5 mol%) retains predominantly isotropic-appearing fields over a similar or modestly expanded lower-temperature range, consistent with altered interfacial interactions without requiring polymeric stabilizers. At higher Eu-DTPA-PE contents (≥5-12.5 mol%), the PLM micrographs exhibit increasingly extensive birefringent textures across the temperature series, although fixed-threshold image analysis identifies formulation-specific abrupt, broad, or nonpersistent changes rather than a single monotonic loading-dependent birefringence-onset sequence. DLS showed that the formulations remained submicron, colloidally stable lipid-particle dispersions across the full Eu-DTPA-PE loading series. Steady-state Eu 3+ fluorescence revealed substantially enhanced emission for Eu-DTPA-PE lipid-particle formulations relative to aqueous EuCl 3 , indicating a formulation-dependent Eu 3+ emission response. The increased luminescence is consistent with a changed local Eu 3+ environment and altered nonradiative quenching within the lipid assemblies; however, steady-state emission alone does not independently establish local hydration or coordination geometry. For the 10 and 12.5 mol% Eu-DTPA-PE (18 : 0) formulations, integrated Eu 3+ emission normalized to ICP-MS-determined Eu concentration was similar, indicating that the greater raw emission at 12.5 mol% was largely explained by its greater Eu content. Together with earlier Gd-DTPA monoolein submicron lipid particles, these results establish lanthanide-chelating lipids as a modular platform in which chelator-lipid composition can modulate temperature-dependent birefringence and Eu 3+ photophysical behavior in polymer-free monoolein-based submicron lipid particles.

article.title: Tumor-on-a-chip with single-cell microfluidics reveals distinct NK cell immunosuppression by hypoxia versus lipid accumulation.
article.authors: Wang A, Wang Y, Han X, Chen Q, Liu W.
article.abstract: Immunosuppression induced by metabolic stress within the solid tumor microenvironment (TME) critically limits the efficacy of cancer immunotherapies. Here, we develop a tumor microenvironment-on-a-chip (TMoC) platform integrated with single-cell microfluidic analysis to precisely model both hypoxic and lipid-enriched conditions commonly found in solid tumors. Utilizing this system, we elucidate the distinct effects of these two metabolic stressors on natural killer (NK) cell function. Hypoxia broadly suppresses NK cell cytotoxicity and downregulates multiple functional molecules. In contrast, lipid accumulation exerts a selective inhibitory effect, reducing granzyme B and IL-10 expression while relatively preserving IFN-γ mRNA expression. Single-cell analysis reveals stress-induced functional heterogeneity and secretory synergy among NK cells. Notably, we identified a relatively high-IFN-γ-secreting subpopulation retained under lipid-rich conditions despite an overall reduction in IFN-γ secretion at the single-cell level. Furthermore, single-cell pairing assays dissociate global killing efficacy from killing kinetics, revealing that hypoxia and lipid accumulation impair NK cells through distinct kinetic modes. Using the TMoC platform to evaluate combination therapies targeting both hypoxia and lipid metabolism, we show that dual intervention synergistically restores NK cell cytolytic function. The platform demonstrates superior screening sensitivity compared to conventional in vitro models. Collectively, this work highlights the potential of integrating engineered microphysiological systems with single-cell analysis to decipher complex TME interactions and guide the development of immunotherapeutic strategies.

article.title: Genomic Profile of Asian Women with Recurrent Implantation Failure: A Systematic Review.
article.authors: Sini KPI, Temenggung NAA, Handayani N, Loedin AK, Sini IR.
article.abstract: Recurrent implantation failure is a major challenge in assisted reproductive technology, affecting up to 15% of women undergoing in vitro fertilization. Although several hypotheses for the pathogenesis of the condition have been proposed, many RIF cases remain unexplained. Studies have suggested potential genomic contributions to RIF. However, most studies have focused on non-Asian or mixed populations, leaving gaps in understanding population-specific genetic risks. This systematic review aimed to characterize the genomic profile of Asian women with RIF and identify candidate genetic variants associated with increased susceptibility. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, OVID, and ScienceDirect up to June 2025 for case-control studies analyzing genetic polymorphisms in Asian women diagnosed with RIF. Five eligible studies were identified, comprising 566 women with RIF and 732 fertile controls from East and West Asia. Variants in genes related to angiogenesis (VEGF), RNA interference (AGO2), lipid transport (APOE), folate metabolism (MTHFR, TYMS/TS), and DNA repair (MDM2) were identified. Consistent associations were observed for VEGF polymorphisms (rs833061, rs25648, rs1570360) and AGO2 rs4961280, reported up to two-fold higher risk of RIF, while APOE ε4 carriage was linked to a similar increase. Combined MTHFR and TYMS genotypes also showed additive effects on RIF susceptibility. Genetic variants affecting angiogenesis, RNA processing, and lipid metabolism may contribute to RIF pathogenesis in Asian women. VEGF emerged as the most consistently associated gene, highlighting the importance of endometrial vascular remodeling in implantation success. Larger, multi-ethnic genomic studies with functional validation, together with a standardized definition of RIF, are warranted to clarify these associations and advance personalized reproductive medicine in ART.

article.title: Pixel classifier-based image analysis of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis in mice.
article.authors: Lee Y, Bergin IL, Blok NB, Myronovych A, McMahon G, Seeley RJ, Bozadjieva-Kramer N.
article.abstract: Image analysis in histologic assessments has increasingly gained traction in comparative pathology and biomedical research. However, application has been limited by a knowledge gap, particularly for veterinary pathologists without a strong background in coding-intensive image analysis. This study describes a quantitative image analysis pipeline for liver pathology in a special diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) mouse model, using the existing open-source, graphic user interface-based program QuPath. A machine learning-based pixel classifier was trained on annotations made in 7 digitized hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained slides to detect normal hepatocytes, macrosteatosis, microsteatosis, vessels, and inflammation. Macrosteatosis annotations were then segmented via pixel thresholding to quantify lipid droplets. Post-processing pixel thresholding was applied to quantify fibrosis in picrosirius red-stained slides and lipid droplets in H&E-stained slides. Results were benchmarked against traditional manual grading by the nonalcoholic steatohepatitis activity score (NAS). Our results revealed a significantly larger macrosteatosis area percentage in MASH diet mice than in regular diet controls. The percentage areas for steatosis, inflammation, and fibrosis strongly correlated with increasing histopathologic scores. Unlike traditional ordinal severity scoring like NAS, this approach generates continuous, quantitative data suitable for parametric statistical analysis. This method is scalable and accessible, requires no coding expertise or commercial software, and offers a blueprint for generating truly quantitative histopathology data to veterinary pathologists and others engaged in MASH research.

article.title: Uncovering the lymphatic uptake, pharmacokinetics, and biodistribution of mRNA-lipid nanoparticles after intravenous and subcutaneous injection.
article.authors: Li P, Abdallah M, Yao Y, Mugan RS, Payne TJ, Fabb SA, Pouton CW, Trevaskis NL.
article.venue: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
article.abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulations have enabled the in vivo delivery of messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) vaccines and therapeutics yet the delivery of RNA remains relatively inefficient. In order to improve LNP design there is a need to better understand how current mRNA-LNP formulations are trafficked and expressed in vivo. Importantly, no prior work has quantified mRNA-LNP transport through lymphatics. In the current study we profile the thoracic lymph uptake, plasma pharmacokinetics (PK), and tissue protein expression after intravenous (IV) and subcutaneous (SC) administration in rats of three common LNP formulations (ALC-0315, SM-102 and MC3 ionizable lipids) containing muGFP-P2A-nLuc reporter mRNA. After IV administration, the SM-102 and MC3 LNP formulations provided the most effective protection of mRNA in plasma. Despite this, tissue NanoLuc® Luciferase (nLuc) expression at 32 h post-dosing was relatively similar across formulations with highest expression seen in the liver and spleen. After SC injection, all formulations supported relatively low bioavailability of mRNA (0.42-0.87% dose) and slightly higher bioavailability of ionizable and PEG lipid (<5% dose) with PK profiles of the ionizable lipid and PEG lipid not completely matching the mRNA PK profiles. There was also greater lymphatic recovery of all ionizable lipids (3.1-4.3% dose) compared to mRNA (0.62-1.4% dose) and PEG lipid (1.9-2.0% dose). Together this data suggests that mRNA is lost prior to or during lymphatic transport. Importantly, concentrations of all mRNA-LNP components were 10-1000 fold higher in thoracic lymph compared to plasma after SC injection. At 32 h after SC injection, highest nLuc expression was seen in lymph nodes and tissues near the dosing site and in the liver and spleen. These findings demonstrating that mRNA-LNPs predominantly traffic from tissue injection sites via lymphatics, mRNA-LNP components may traffic separately from each other in both lymph and blood, and tissue protein expression reflects the PK of mRNA-LNPs at early timepoints.

article.title: A lipid-related metabolic signature of the dietary index for gut microbiota predicts a lower risk of osteoarthritis.
article.authors: Xia H, Song X, Xiang R, Zhang D, Liu T, Ma X, Yang B, Zhong Y, Xia M, Ju Y, Chen Z, Pang Y, Li Z, Fan M, Jiang X.
article.abstract: Aims To identify a metabolic signature linked to the dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) and examine its association with the risk of osteoarthritis (OA), while accounting for genetic predispositions. Methods We analyzed data from 97,569 UK Biobank participants. An elastic net regression model was used to derive a DI-GM-related metabolic signature from circulating metabolites. Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations of the DI-GM and its metabolic signature with OA risk. A polygenic risk score (PRS) for OA was incorporated to examine joint associations and potential gene-environment interactions. Mediation and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were used to explore metabolic pathways potentially mediating the DI-GM-OA association. Results During a median follow-up of 11.6 years, 12,860 incident cases of all OA and 4,392 cases of knee OA were documented. Higher DI-GM was associated with lower risks of all OA (HR = 0.94, 95%CIs = 0.90-0.98) and knee OA (HR = 0.91, 95%CIs = 0.84-0.99). The DI-GM-related metabolic signature showed stronger inverse associations, with participants in the highest versus lowest tertile having substantially lower risks of all OA (HR = 0.77, 95%CIs = 0.73-0.80) and knee OA (HR = 0.66, 95%CIs = 0.61-0.72). These associations remained robust after mutual adjustment and were consistent across different levels of genetic susceptibility, with joint analyses suggesting that favorable metabolic profiles were associated with attenuated OA risk. Mediation analyses suggested a potential role for lipid-related metabolism in the DI-GM-OA association, with MR providing additional evidence for specific metabolic associations. Conclusions We identified a robust DI-GM-related metabolic signature that was inversely associated with OA risk. Notably, favorable metabolic profiles were associated with attenuated OA risk among individuals with high genetic susceptibility.

article.title: Machine learning-guided chondrocyte membrane-camouflaged lipid nanoparticles for intra-articular SOX9 mRNA therapy of osteoarthritis.
article.authors: Li J, Li C, Wang H, Yu H, Zhang T, Li C, Wang X, Peng Y.
article.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) progression involves cartilage matrix loss and persistent inflammation. This study developed a machine learning-guided and chondrocyte membrane-camouflaged lipid nanoparticle carrying messenger RNA (CM-LNP@mRNA) platform for intra-articular SOX9 delivery. Random forest analysis identified the nitrogen-to-phosphorus and SM-102 ratios as primary determinants with feature importance values of 0.57 and 0.32 respectively. Following ML-guided formulation selection and experimental membrane-coating optimization, the final CM-LNP@mRNA formulation showed an encapsulation efficiency of 95.50% and a particle size of 133.70 nm. Compared with the conventional reference formulation prepared under the same final coating condition, encapsulation efficiency increased from 89.20% to 95.50% and particle size decreased from 145.40 nm to 133.70 nm. Membrane coating shifted the zeta potential from -25.57 mV to -35.07 mV. This transition provided biophysical evidence of successful surface modification. In interleukin-1β-stimulated chondrocytes, CM-LNP@mRNA increased the relative expression of Col2a1 and Acan from 0.20 to 0.33 and from 0.50 to 0.73, respectively, while reducing the relative expression of Mmp3 and Adamts5 from 10.50 to 7.80 and from 4.00 to 2.50, respectively. These alterations indicated a shift toward a matrix-preserving transcriptional state. Downstream matrix metalloproteinase 3 and prostaglandin E2 concentrations decreased from 37.10 ng/mL to 18.50 ng/mL and from 113.70 pg/mL to 76.50 pg/mL by day 7. This reduction demonstrated effective suppression of catabolic and inflammatory activity. In OA rats, CM-LNP@mRNA reduced the osteophyte volume from 4.00 mm 3 to 2.00 mm 3 and prolonged the thermal response latency from 7.50 s to 11.80 s. These improvements linked cellular metabolic regulation to functional joint recovery. These findings establish a strategy integrating formulation optimization with biomimetic membrane coating to modulate the OA microenvironment.

article.title: Gain-of-Function Variants in PLAAT4 and Spinal Predominant Demyelinating Leukodystrophy.
article.authors: Zeng YH, Chen B, Shi Y, Jiang J, Zhang Z, Ma MM, Wu S, Fu J, Zhang S, Lin J, Ye P, Chen S, Yan X, Zhu J, Xie J, Lin S, Dong E, Cheng X, Wang N, Ke R, Li R, Shui G, Yong VW, Chen WJ, Lin X.
article.abstract: Importance Leukoencephalopathies are clinically and etiologically heterogeneous disorders, and establishing a specific diagnosis remains challenging. Patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and brain white matter hyperintensities (WMH) may be misdiagnosed as having multiple sclerosis, potentially exposing them to unnecessary immunosuppressive therapy. Objective To define the clinical, radiological, and genetic features of spinal predominant demyelinating leukodystrophy with leg spasticity (SPDMLS). Design, setting, and participants This case series involved participants from 4 tertiary referral hospitals within the China Alliance for Rare Diseases during the period July 2019 to August 2025. The study design integrated clinical evaluations and whole-exome sequencing (WES), as well as targeted plasma lipidomics correlated with SPATAX-EUROSPA disability stages. Variant pathogenicity was evaluated using an oligodendrocyte-specific knock-in mouse model. Participants were patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and central nervous system (CNS) WMH and available family members, including presymptomatic carriers. Exposures WES, genetic characterization, testing. Main outcomes and measures Identification of disease-associated gene and characterization of clinical, radiological, and genetic features of SPDMLS. Results Twenty-six individuals from 11 unrelated families were included; 4 patients underwent longitudinal follow-up for up to 5 years. Recurrent heterozygous PLAAT4 (phospholipase A and acyltransferase 4) variants (p.I14T and p.A96V) were associated with a novel autosomal dominant leukoencephalopathy, named SPDMLS. Age at onset was 11 to 51 years (median [IQR], 22 [15-29] years), with patients predominantly developing spastic paraplegia. Symbol Digit Modalities Test scores ranged from 11 to 70 in 6 available patients. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated slow progression with heterogeneous brain WMH and a stereotyped pattern of symmetric, long-segment "girdle-like" spinal cord WMH accompanied by atrophy. Somatosensory- and motor-evoked potentials indicated dysfunction of the dorsal columns and corticospinal tracts, respectively. In presymptomatic carriers, spinal cord signal alterations preceded brain involvement. An oligodendrocyte-specific knock-in mouse model provided in vivo functional evidence supporting a role of PLAAT4 gain-of-function in driving demyelination, informing SPDMLS pathogenesis. Patient plasma lipidomics suggested accumulation of arachidonic acid-related lipids correlating with disability stage. Conclusions and relevance This study found that PLAAT4 variants delineated SPDMLS, a clinically distinct leukodystrophy that should be considered in patients with unexplained spastic paraplegia and CNS WMH. Arachidonic acid-related lipids represent a candidate biomarker for disease progression.

article.title: Single-cell analysis of 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD)-treated murine skin demonstrates that sebaceous gland differentiation precedes Ahr-dependent seboatrophy, with elevated expression of infundibular Blimp1.
article.authors: Tasnim SM, Solanki S, Bhuju J, Thompson L, Skalli O, Grice EA, Sutter CH, Sutter TR.
article.venue: Toxicological sciences : an official journal of the Society of Toxicology
article.abstract: In humans, 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) induces chloracne, a skin condition that presents with acanthosis, hyperkeratosis, sebaceous gland (SG) atrophy (seboatrophy), and hamartomas. Although chloracne-like phenotypes have been reported in TCDD-treated mice, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Previous studies showed that TCDD-induced CYP1A1 protein is expressed in LRIG1+ progenitor cells in hair follicles, suggesting that TCDD targets specific cell populations within the pilosebaceous unit. To explore the effects of TCDD on the epidermis and pilosebaceous unit, we analyzed single-cell RNA expression in wild-type and Ahr-null mice at postnatal day 21 (P21) following in utero and lactational exposure. The results showed that TCDD preferentially induced the AHR target genes Cyp1a1 and Cyp1b1 in the lower infundibulum and subjacent junctional zone overlapping the LRIG1+ progenitor cell niche. TCDD also caused Ahr-dependent seboatrophy, accompanied by increased expression of Blimp1, a transcriptional repressor that regulates SG size. A second site of Cyp1a1 induction was the SG, where Cyp1a1 was markedly elevated in the basal proliferating cells and immature sebocytes. In a 3-day topical exposure study of early effects, TCDD produced a dose-dependent increase of Cyp1a1 expression in the SG that included the more differentiated sebocytes. This response was accompanied by expansion of the Scd1-positive area, elevated Nile Red lipid staining, and an increased number of Blimp1-high sebocytes, demonstrating that TCDD enhanced SG differentiation and lipid production in vivo. These changes preceded the onset of Ahr-dependent seboatrophy, providing new insight into the cellular and molecular events underlying chloracne pathogenesis.

article.title: Physicochemical Characterization and In Vitro Evaluation of Praziquantel-loaded Oleogels for Oral Drug Delivery.
article.authors: Nsanzubuhoro C, Tai SL, Robert Wm Pott.
article.abstract: Oral delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs such as praziquantel (PZQ) is frequently limited by poor absorption and low bioavailability. Lipid-based carriers represent a promising strategy, as their matrices enhance solubility by incorporating hydrophobic molecules within a lipophilic environment. In this study, PZQ-loaded beeswax (BW) oleogels were formulated using palm oil (PO) or cottonseed oil (CSO) as lipid carriers, followed by physicochemical characterisation and in vitro studies. We hypothesised that differences in oil composition would influence the structure and physicochemical properties of BW oleogels, affecting drug release, in vitro digestion behaviour, and intestinal permeation. BW oleogels exhibited gelation at a critical concentration of 5% (w/w), resulting in a high oil-binding capacity of at least 98%. Microscopy and X-ray diffraction indicated concentration-dependent development of a dense, needle-like semi-crystalline network, while rheological analysis confirmed stable gel behaviour (G' > G″). For the first time, we demonstrate the application of a modified everted gut sac model, adapted to quantitatively investigate the intestinal interaction and permeation behaviour of PZQ-loaded oleogels. Simulated in vitro digestion revealed negligible release under salivary conditions and limited gastric release (< 16%), followed by a bioaccessible fraction of 52-57%. The BW oleogels exhibited reduced intestinal permeation relative to the free drug, indicating drug entrapment within the oleogel, while oleogel-intestinal tissue interaction remained below 7.8%. These findings highlight the potential of BW oleogels as oral carriers for hydrophobic compounds such as PZQ and suggest their applicability as modified-release delivery systems.

article.title: Protein palmitoylation in disease: decoding its crosstalk with ubiquitination and phosphorylation for pathogenic mechanisms and targeted therapeutics.
article.authors: Li S, Suo H, Hao R, Wu R, Liang Y, Kong E, Cao L, Zhou B.
article.venue: Journal of genetics and genomics = Yi chuan xue bao
article.abstract: Protein S-palmitoylation is a reversible lipid modification that governs protein stability, trafficking, and signaling. Rather than an isolated tag, it acts as a spatiotemporal routing signal within an integrated post-translational modification (PTM) network, engaging in three defined crosstalk modes with ubiquitination and phosphorylation: synergistic, antagonistic, and cascading. Although crosstalk with acetylation and myristoylation exists, this review focuses on the ubiquitination- and phosphorylation-centered networks most directly linked to palmitoylation in disease. The same palmitoylation event can stabilize or destabilize substrates, or activate or silence signaling, depending on the specific Zinc finger DHHC domain-containing protein (ZDHHC) isoform, subcellular location, local enzyme availability, and metabolic state. We further introduce the "PTM context signature", a four-variable predictive framework for disease-specific crosstalk outcomes. By dissecting palmitoylation-centered crosstalk through a disease-oriented lens, we examine how its dysregulation drives oncogenesis, inflammation, metabolic disorders, and neurodegeneration. We then translate these mechanistic principles into a network-centric therapeutic framework, evaluating ZDHHC-directed modulators, peptide-based interface disruptors, and crosstalk-informed combinations that target context-specific nodes and anticipate therapy resistance. Viewing palmitoylation as an integrated component of the cellular PTM network, rather than as an isolated lipid tag, provides a framework for understanding disease pathogenesis and for targeting PTM networks rather than single modifications.

article.title: Second-Generation Combined Oral Contraceptives Induce Early Cardiovascular Risk Through Inflammatory and Oxidative Vascular Remodeling.
article.authors: Allen MO, Salami SA, Olumide OM, Lawal-Bamidele OA, Murtala BA.
article.abstract: Second-generation combined oral contraceptive pills (COCPs), particularly formulations containing ethinylestradiol and levonorgestrel, remain widely used because of their effectiveness and affordability in middle and low-income countries. However, concerns persist about their cardiovascular safety. This study investigated the dose-dependent effects of a second-generation COCP on systolic blood pressure (SBP), inflammatory biomarkers, oxidative stress, vascular mediators, and vascular histology in female Sprague-Dawley rats. Twenty-four female Sprague-Dawley rats were acclimatized and randomly assigned to control, low-dose (1.1 µg/kg/day), and high-dose COCP (11 µg/kg/day) groups. Treatments were administered orally for six weeks. SBP and body weight were monitored before and after treatment. Serum C-reactive protein (CRP), tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), and lipid profile were measured. Renal vascular homogenates were analyzed for nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), endothelin-1 (ET-1), nitric oxide (NO), malondialdehyde (MDA), superoxide dismutase, catalase (CAT), and glutathione. Histological examination was performed on the renal and thoracic arteries. The SBP increased by 4.6% in the low dose and 21.8% in the high dose (p < 0.05). High-dose treatment significantly increased CRP, TNF-α, and NF-κB levels, indicating enhanced systemic and vascular inflammation. Vascular MDA and CAT increased in both treated groups, suggesting oxidative stress with compensatory antioxidant activation. Low-dose COCP increased ET-1 levels, while the NO and lipid profiles showed no significant changes across the treated groups. Both doses produced marked structural alterations in the renal and thoracic arteries. The dose-dependent rise in vascular inflammation, oxidative stress, and SBP suggests early cardiovascular risk is mediated primarily by inflammatory vascular remodeling rather than by overt dyslipidemia.

article.title: Quantifying protein release from hydrophobic ion pairs by cation exchange chromatography.
article.authors: Mu J, Carmali S.
article.venue: Analytical methods : advancing methods and applications
article.abstract: Hydrophobic ion pairing is an established solubility engineering strategy for small molecules and peptides, but its extension to proteins remains comparatively underexplored, and quantitative methods for measuring protein release from these complexes under biorelevant conditions remain limited. Colorimetric and UV-based assays are subject to interference from co-formulated surfactants, bile salts and phospholipids. Here, we report a cation exchange chromatographic method, implemented on a fast protein liquid chromatography system, that separates lysozyme from these matrix components prior to UV detection. Validation in accordance with ICH Q2(R2) demonstrated linearity from 20 to 320 µg mL -1 ( R 2 of 0.9998), a detection limit of 7 µg mL -1 , a quantitation limit of 20 µg mL -1 , and recovery of 88.2% in high ionic-strength media. Recovery decreased to 42.6% in phospholipid-containing media, limiting absolute quantification under these conditions and supporting comparative assessment of protein release. Applied to lysozyme-sodium dodecyl sulphate and lysozyme-dioctyl sulfosuccinate complexes, the method resolved markedly different dissociation behaviour as a function of pH, ionic strength, and simulated intestinal fluid components. Lysozyme-sodium dodecyl sulphate released measurable protein under all conditions, whereas the more stable lysozyme-dioctyl sulfosuccinate complex resisted dissociation, with released lysozyme below the quantitation limit under most simulated intestinal conditions. Recovered lysozyme retained 17-40% of the catalytic activity of native lysozyme depending on the dissociation medium, demonstrating that chromatographic separation enables both quantification and functional assessment of released protein.

article.title: TcFur1, a furin 1 ortholog in Tribolium castaneum, regulates reproduction and carbohydrate metabolism without affecting lipid homeostasis.
article.authors: Sanches-Almeida J, Porto LL, Majerowicz D.
article.abstract: Proprotein convertases of the subtilase family process protein precursors and regulate essential biological processes, including development, metabolism and reproduction. The role of furin 1 (Fur1) in insects remains poorly understood, especially in Tribolium castaneum, a major pest of stored grains. This study describes the TcFur1 ortholog and investigates its effects on development, reproduction and energy metabolism. Phylogenetic analyses establish that TcFur1 is a 1:1 ortholog of type 1 furins from other insects. Quantitative PCR (qPCR) expression profiling indicates that TcFur1 is most highly expressed during the pupal stage, denoting a role in metamorphosis. RNA interference (RNAi)-mediated gene knockdown does not affect viability or development but markedly decreases oviposition in adult females. Triacylglycerol levels and total lipase activity remain unchanged, indicating that TcFur1 is not essential for lipid homeostasis under these conditions. In contrast, TcFur1 knockdown increases circulating trehalose and reduces transcript levels of insulin-like peptides (TcILP1 and TcILP2) and the adipokinetic hormone receptor (TcAKHR), as determined by qPCR. While the corresponding protein levels were not measured due to the lack of specific antibodies, these transcriptional changes are consistent with a role for TcFur1 in the endocrine regulation of carbohydrate metabolism. These results show that TcFur1 is involved in carbohydrate homeostasis and reproduction in T. castaneum, likely through insulin and AKH signalling, without directly affecting lipid metabolism. This data expands the current understanding of proprotein convertase functions in insects and suggests that TcFur1 may serve as a target for RNAi-based population control.

article.title: Melatonin suppresses astrocyte reactivity and Mitigates cognitive deficits induced by a high-carbohydrate, high-fat diet in rats.
article.authors: Dorranipour D, Zangiabadi I, Peyvandi M, Naraki K, Basiri M.
article.abstract: Background High-carbohydrate and high-fat (HCHF) diets may impair cognitive function through neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and astrocyte activation. This study investigated the effects of melatonin on memory impairment and astrocyte reactivity in rats with diet-induced metabolic syndrome. Methods and results Adult male Wistar rats were fed an HCHF diet for eight weeks, followed by daily oral melatonin treatment (5, 10, or 30 mg/kg) for four weeks while continuing the diet. Working memory was assessed using the Y-maze spontaneous alternation test. Hippocampal and hypothalamic tissues were evaluated for proinflammatory cytokines, oxidative stress markers, and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunoreactivity. HCHF feeding caused weight gain, dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, impaired working memory, increased neuroinflammation and oxidative damage, and astrogliosis in both brain regions. Melatonin did not improve glucose tolerance or lipid profiles at any dose. However, working memory performance in melatonin-treated rats was comparable to that of controls at all doses. Melatonin also reduced GFAP-positive astrocytes, proinflammatory cytokine levels, and lipid peroxidation, while increasing superoxide dismutase activity. These effects were mainly dose-dependent in the hippocampus, whereas memory improvement showed no clear dose-dependent pattern. Conclusions Melatonin improved working memory and reduced astrocyte reactivity, neuroinflammation, and oxidative stress in rats fed an HCHF diet, without improving systemic metabolic abnormalities. These findings suggest that melatonin may protect against diet-induced brain injury through mechanisms related to astrocyte activation, inflammation, and oxidative stress.

article.title: Inhibition of the lipid peroxidation and glutathione peroxidase-like activity of 2-methyl benzoselenazoles.
article.authors: Sodhi N, Kadian R, Baschieri A, Amorati R, Jin Z, Madaan K, Singh VP.
article.abstract: 2-Methyl benzoselenazoles were synthesized via the reaction of in situ -generated sodium selenolate with acetyl chloride at room temperature. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirmed a nearly planar structure due to non-bonding Se⋯O interactions, supported by computational analyses. All compounds exhibited good glutathione peroxidase-like antioxidant activity in a coupled reductase assay, as compared to the reference, ebselen. The most active compound was further evaluated under varying concentrations of glutathione to gain deeper insights into its catalytic efficiency. 77 Se{ 1 H} NMR mechanistic study was performed to provide evidence for the key intermediates involved in the decomposition of peroxide. The radical-trapping antioxidant activity of benzoselenazoles was evaluated by the inhibition of azo-initiated autoxidation of cumene in chlorobenzene. It showed peroxyl radical-trapping capability, with an inhibition constant of 1.4 × 10 3 M -1 s -1 and a stoichiometric factor ( n ) ≈ 2, due to H-atom transfer from the amide group, as further confirmed by theoretical calculations. In addition to their antioxidant activities, molecular dynamics studies revealed favourable binding interactions with vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR-2), suggesting dual antioxidant and anti-angiogenic roles.

article.title: Liver function following preterm birth: long-term implications for metabolic health.
article.authors: Yakubu I, Berry MJ, Dyson RM, Gray C.
article.venue: Journal of developmental origins of health and disease
article.abstract: Preterm birth affects one in ten infants and represents one of the major early life insults with long-term health implications. Among the organs most disrupted is the liver, crucial for metabolism, detoxification and general systemic function. While the early clinical signs like neonatal cholestasis are well documented, the molecular mechanisms underlying hepatic dysfunction remain poorly characterised. In this review, we explore the potential hepatic molecular alterations associated with preterm birth that may influence early life programming of metabolic dysfunction. First, we present normal liver function and the potential effect of preterm birth on liver development and function. Second, we review metabolic adaptation in the neonatal period following preterm birth and highlight findings of perturbed circulating and tissue metabolites in both preterm human cohorts and animal models. These altered metabolites are associated with disruption of glucose and insulin homeostasis; alterations in lipid metabolism and lipoprotein profiles; impaired bile acid metabolism; perturbations in amino acid and protein metabolism; oxidative stress and antioxidant imbalance; as well as hormonal, growth factor and immune dysregulation. Finally, we examine whether these metabolic perturbations resolve or persist during maturation and consider their potential contribution to adverse metabolic outcomes later in life. Although many of the metabolic perturbations appear to normalise, evidence suggests persistent alterations in insulin signalling and lipid metabolism. Despite growing evidence across the life course following preterm birth, the molecular mechanisms linking early hepatic alterations with later adverse metabolic outcomes remain poorly defined. Epidemiological studies nevertheless demonstrate increased risks of insulin resistance, dyslipidaemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and type 2 diabetes in individuals born preterm.

article.title: From Interfacial Films to Vesicles: Interactions of Dapagliflozin with Tween 20-Modified Lipid Membranes and Their Implications for Encapsulation in Transferosomes.
article.authors: Wilczewska K, Pawlikowski M, Kołodziejczak-Radzimska A, Dopierała K.
article.abstract: Understanding drug-lipid interactions is essential for the rational design of lipid-based nanocarriers. Dapagliflozin (DAPA), a highly selective sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor with expanding therapeutic applications, represents an attractive candidate for lipid-based delivery systems; however, the physicochemical basis of its interactions with lipid membranes remains insufficiently understood. In this study, Langmuir monolayers and lipid vesicles were employed as complementary systems to investigate DAPA-lipid interactions and their modulation by the edge activator Tween 20. Langmuir monolayer experiments demonstrated that DAPA markedly affected lipid packing, compressional properties, and relaxation behavior. Importantly, these effects depended on the presence of Tween 20, revealing a composition-dependent interplay between the drug, lipids, and edge activator rather than independent effects of the individual components. The interfacial studies also showed that the role of Tween 20 cannot be described solely in terms of monolayer fluidization. DAPA-loaded liposomes and Tween 20-containing transferosomes exhibited high apparent encapsulation efficiencies. DAPA markedly altered the particle-size distributions of both formulations, producing a multimodal distribution in liposomes and shifting the predominant intensity-weighted population of transferosomes toward the micrometer range. AFM measurements further demonstrated pronounced changes in vesicle nanomechanics, with both DAPA and Tween 20 reducing stiffness and Young's modulus relative to empty liposomes. Adhesion parameters increased when DAPA was encapsulated in the vesicles. Overall, the combined monolayer-vesicle approach reveals a composition-dependent interplay between DAPA, lipids, and Tween 20 that governs interfacial organization, particle-size distribution, and nanomechanical behavior. These findings highlight the importance of considering the drug as an active contributor to membrane properties rather than merely an encapsulated cargo and provide a physicochemical basis for further optimization of DAPA-containing transferosomal systems.

article.title: Enhancing mRNA-lipid nanoparticle vaccine-induced T cell responses by simple supplementation with class B CpG oligodeoxynucleotides.
article.authors: Hirata H, Abe Y, Itoh Y, Hirai T, Yoshioka Y.
article.abstract: mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (LNP) vaccines can elicit robust T cell responses; however, these responses remain insufficient, particularly in the context of cancer vaccine therapy. Although several types of adjuvants reportedly enhance T cell responses induced by mRNA-LNP vaccines, few comprehensive side-by-side comparisons exist, and it remains unclear which adjuvants are most suitable. Herein, we screened 15 adjuvants. The addition of class B CpG oligodeoxynucleotides (ODNs) markedly augmented T cell induction in an interleukin-12-dependent manner and promoted the antitumor effects of mRNA-LNP vaccines in mice. Class B CpG ODN-adjuvanted mRNA-LNP vaccines induced more potent T cell responses than the mRNA-LNP vaccine administered at a 10-fold higher dose, while exhibiting a more favorable safety profile. However, this approach also reduced the cellular uptake of mRNA-LNPs and antigen expression. As a possible mechanism underlying this reduced delivery efficiency, we found that class B CpG ODNs adsorbed onto LNPs and altered their particle characteristics. These findings demonstrate that supplementation with class B CpG ODN is a simple, safe, and readily implementable approach for enhancing mRNA-LNP vaccine-induced T cell responses. This study also highlights that adding auxiliary components to mRNA-LNPs can potentially affect the performance of LNPs as delivery carriers.

article.title: PIAS3 CircRNA-Loaded Lipid Nanoparticles Restore ALOX15 SUMOylation to Suppress Cementoblast Ferroptosis and Attenuate Orthodontically Induced Root Resorption.
article.authors: Hou Y, Yan C, Xu X, Yang Z, Wu X, Zhao H, Song X, Zhang J, Li Y, Yang A, Lu X, Liu Y.
article.abstract: Excessive orthodontic compression induces cementoblast dysfunction and contributes to orthodontically induced root resorption (OIRR), yet the molecular mechanisms linking mechanical stress to cementoblast ferroptosis remain unclear. Compression-induced PIAS3 loss attenuates SUMO3-dependent ALOX15 SUMOylation and impairs ALOX15 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, thereby promoting lipid peroxidation and cementoblast ferroptosis. Based on these findings, PIAS3 circRNA-loaded uridine-derived lipid nanoparticles (PIAS3-OLNPs) were developed, which efficiently restored PIAS3 expression and inhibited cementoblast ferroptosis and subsequent osteoclast differentiation. Moreover, the incorporation of PIAS3-OLNPs into an injectable F127DA hydrogel prolonged local retention and sustained PIAS3 expression in the gingival sulcus, thereby inhibiting cementoblast ferroptosis and osteoclastogenesis and preserving root integrity in vivo. Collectively, this study establishes PIAS3-mediated ALOX15 SUMOylation as a key mechanism that restrains cementoblast ferroptosis and demonstrates that restoring this pathway through local PIAS3 circRNA delivery offers a therapeutic strategy for OIRR and potentially other ferroptosis-related disorders.

article.title: Disulfide bond-modified ionizable lipids for co-delivery of siRNA and carbon dots in the treatment of acute liver injury.
article.authors: Chu R, Shen Z, Pan T, Gao Q, Wang Z, He J.
article.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe clinical condition characterized by excessive oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, for which effective targeted therapeutic strategies remain limited. In this study, a redox-responsive ionizable lipid (Lipid S) was designed by incorporating a disulfide bond into its hydrophobic tail. Under reductive conditions, cleavage of the disulfide bond triggered rapid disassembly of the lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), enabling controlled cargo release. Using Lipid S, a nanoplatform (CD-siL@LNP-S) was established by loading small interfering RNA against interleukin-11 receptor alpha-1 (siIL11ra1) onto carbon dots (CDs) and encapsulating the resulting complex within lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). CD-siL@LNP-S exhibited stable physicochemical properties, efficiently silenced IL11ra1 expression, and reduced reactive oxygen species (ROS) production without inducing cytotoxicity. In an acetaminophen-induced ALI mouse model, the formulation preferentially accumulated in the liver and was efficiently taken up by hepatocytes, resulting in significant attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and tissue injury while maintaining good systemic safety. Overall, Lipid S provides a simple and effective strategy for redox-responsive nucleic acid delivery, and CD-siL@LNP-S represents a promising therapeutic approach for oxidative stress-related liver diseases and other conditions with reductive intracellular environments.

article.title: Beyond a Single Mechanism: The iron-ROS-lipid Peroxidation Axis as a Central Driver of Prodromal Parkinson's Disease.
article.authors: Lyu P, Shen W, Wang Y, Chen X, Liu S, Zhang Y, A M, Jia X, Zhang M, Bu N, Wang S, Bai Y.
article.abstract: Neurodegeneration in Parkinson's disease (PD) begins subtly many years before motor symptoms appear. The primary pathological processes involve abnormal aggregation and spread of α-synuclein (α-syn), ongoing glial-mediated neuroinflammation, and disrupted brain iron balance. We suggest that a positive feedback loop involving iron-ROS-lipid peroxidation plays a crucial role in connecting these events and propelling the early stages of PD. Iron overload induces lipid peroxidation through the Fenton reaction, generating products like 4-HNE. These byproducts not only modify α-syn structure but also act as signals that trigger the microglial NLRP3 inflammasome. Additionally, pathological α-syn prompts glial cells to release exosomes containing harmful proteins and oxidized lipids, facilitating the spread of ferroptosis stress between cells and brain regions. This mechanism amplifies damage from single neurons to the entire neural network. This comprehensive framework clarifies the intricate interplay among α-syn pathology, neuroinflammation, and iron imbalance in early PD stages, highlighting ferroptosis as a key driver of disease progression.

article.title: Mating cell traps to silica microbands for picoliter thin layer chromatography (pTLC) assay of phosphoinositide metabolism in single cells.
article.authors: Yao M, Prober MM, Wang Y, Dilley K, Sims CE, Allbritton NL.
article.abstract: The phosphoinositide pathway plays key roles in the survival and proliferation of single tumor cells driving a need for single-cell assays of phosphoinositide signaling. In this work, cell traps aligned over monolithic silica microbands [picoliter thin layer chromatography (pTLC)] were used to place a single cell on microbands within an array with a greater than 70% efficiency. Separation and quantification of the metabolites of BODIPY fluorescein-labelled phosphoinositide 4-phosphate (BODIPY FL PI4P) formed was demonstrated in over 900 single cells using pTLC with cell traps. The major metabolite of BODIPY FL PI4P formed in cells was BODIPY FL phosphatidylinositol (PI) likely due to the actions of the suppressor of actin (SAC) family of phosphoinositide phosphatases. A minor metabolite possessed a migration time similar to that of BODIPY fluorescein-labelled phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (BODIPY FL PI(4,5)P 2 ). On average 59% ± 1% of BODIPY FL PI4P was dephosphorylated in K562 (chronic myelogenous leukemia), while significantly greater dephosphorylation (62% ± 1%) was observed in MM1S (multiple myeloma). In contrast the aggressive cell Kasumi-3 (undifferentiated acute myeloblastic leukemia) displayed significantly greater metabolism (66% ± 2%) of the PI4P reporter than other cell lines. All cell lines assessed displayed large numbers of cells with metabolic behavior far removed from that of the population average, revealing the full extent of cell-based behaviors in the cell population. Immunoassay of trapped Kasumi-3 cells followed by pTLC demonstrated the potential for pairing other assays with pTLC.

article.title: Prioritising determinants of systemic inflammation across molecular, physiological and disease phenotypes.
article.authors: Shepherd, F.; Slaney, C.; Jones, H. J.; Dardani, C.; Stergiakouli, E.; Sanderson, E. C. M.; Hamilton, F.; Rosoff, D. B.; Rek, N.; Gaunt, T. R.; Davey Smith, G.; Richardson, T. G.; Khandaker, G. M.
article.abstract: Background Systemic inflammation has been widely studied as a driver of disease, yet its upstream determinants remain poorly understood. Methods We performed a large-scale two-sample Mendelian randomisation study evaluating potential causal effects of 3,213 molecular, physiological and disease traits on circulating interleukin-6 and C-reactive protein. These comprised 2,923 proteomic, 249 metabolomic, 17 cardiometabolic, 7 neuropsychiatric, 8 immune-mediated inflammatory and 9 infection-related traits. Genetic instruments from genome-wide association studies were analysed using inverse variance weighted, weighted median and MR-Egger methods, with multiple-testing correction. Consistency across methods informed robustness, and bidirectional MR assessed reverse causation. Results After Bonferroni correction, 72 traits showed evidence of potential causal effects on CRP and 9 on IL-6. CRP was predominantly influenced by metabolomic traits, particularly lipid and fatty acid measures. Genetically proxied adiposity (body mass index and obesity), triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, glycoprotein acetyls (GlycA) and apolipoprotein E increased CRP, whereas HDL-related cholesterols, polyunsaturated fatty acids and glutamine decreased CRP. Most associations were consistent across MR methods. IL-6 was primarily influenced by adiposity and HDL-related lipid measures, with generally smaller effects and limited support from sensitivity analyses. Bidirectional analyses provided little evidence that CRP directly drives metabolic traits when restricted to cis-acting instruments, whereas genetically proxied IL-6 signalling showed consistent downstream effects on HDL particle concentration and composition. Conclusions Adiposity is a shared upstream determinant of both biomarkers, with stronger and broader effects on CRP. These findings suggest that CRP integrates downstream systemic inflammatory burden, whereas IL-6 reflects a more tightly regulated, context-dependent process. By shifting the focus from inflammation as a cause to inflammation as a consequence, this study maps potential causal drivers of systemic inflammation across a broad spectrum of traits and pathways, identifies pathways connecting inflammation with cardiometabolic and inflammatory diseases, and provides a resource for prioritising upstream determinants for mechanistic investigation and therapeutic targeting. After Bonferroni correction, evidence of potential causal effects was observed for 72 traits on CRP and 9 traits on IL-6. CRP was predominantly influenced by metabolomic traits, especially lipid and fatty acid measures. Genetically proxied adiposity (body mass index and obesity), triglyceride rich lipoproteins, glycoprotein acetyls (GlycA), and apolipoprotein E increased CRP levels, whereas HDL-related cholesterols, polyunsaturated fatty acids, and glutamine decreased CRP. Most associations were consistent across MR methods, supporting the robustness of these results. As expected, IL-6 had a large effect on CRP. IL-6 was influenced by primarily adiposity and HDL-related lipid measures, with generally smaller effect sizes and limited support across sensitivity analyses. Bidirectional analyses indicated little evidence that CRP directly drives metabolic traits when restricting to cis-acting instruments, whereas genetically proxied IL-6 signalling showed consistent downstream effects on HDL particle concentration and composition. Adiposity is a shared upstream determinant of both inflammatory biomarkers, with stronger and broader effects on CRP. These findings suggest that CRP acts as an integrated downstream readout of systemic inflammatory burden, whereas IL-6 reflects a more tightly regulated and context-dependent process. Our work clarifies traits that may causally influence systemic inflammation and highlights biological pathways linking inflammation to cardiometabolic and inflammatory diseases. By mapping upstream determinants of IL-6 and CRP, we also provide a resource to prioritise key drivers for mechanistic study and therapeutic targeting.

article.title: Curated neurodegeneration axis signals are sensitive to cell composition and analytic choices: an adversarial re-analysis of a transcriptomic scoring pipeline
article.authors: Ghosh, N.; Sinha, K.
article.abstract: Background: Curated gene-set ("axis") scores are widely used to summarise disease biology in postmortem brain transcriptomes. In bulk tissue such scores can also change with cell-type composition, with broad transcriptome shifts in diseased tissue, or with analysis choices made after the results were seen. We tested these explanations on our own published pipeline, NeuroFate, whose preprint reported an Alzheimer's disease (AD) "neuronal vulnerability" axis and a Parkinson's disease (PD) "divergent" synuclein-mitochondrial axis. Results: A code audit found that the AD discovery axis averaged Sst, Pvalb and Lamp5 interneuron cell-type proportions together with its gene-expression features; that 90 endpoint x axis tests were run before the endpoints were locked; that axes were defined from the cohorts later cited as discovery evidence; and that the PD-divergent label came from an axis-specific rule defined after the result. Their contribution to the AD association could not be quantified because the donor-level data were not archived. In GSE7621 (16 PD, 9 controls) the synuclein-mitochondrial association reproduced (exact p = 0.0011) but depended on the scoring method (exact p from 0.001 to 0.057; with per-gene standardisation no axis reached Benjamini-Hochberg significance), lay at the 2.4th percentile of 10,000 expression-matched random probe sets (two-sided p = 0.06), and was attenuated by 76% (95% interval 26% to >100%) after adjustment for a dopaminergic-marker expression proxy (PD coefficient -1.13 to -0.27 SD). A small laser-captured cohort (GSE20141; 10 PD, 8 controls) was inconclusive: no axis reached p < 0.05, and the synuclein-mitochondrial effect had the same sign. In 1,000 simulated cohorts, a naive test called a purely composition-driven gene set significant in 82% of cohorts, whereas the proposed battery classified it as composition-independent in 5% while recovering a planted within-cell effect in 98% (moderate effect) and 50% (weak effect) of cohorts. Conclusions: The original axis associations do not establish composition-independent disease programs; their interpretation is sensitive to feature construction, scoring and adjustment for cell composition. Curated axis scores in bulk brain tissue should be reported with competitive null distributions, composition adjustment, exact small-sample inference, and endpoints and scoring fixed before analysis. We provide code for these checks.

article.title: Hepatic urea cycle suppression drives brown fat thermogenesis to counter obesity and liver disease
article.authors: Kim, L. C.; Lesner, N. P.; Cai, X.; Han, X.; Xu, J. P.; Zhao, A.; Coffey, N. J.; Zheng, D.; Keith, B.; Mesaros, C.; Arany, Z.; Simon, M. C.
article.abstract: The hepatic urea cycle is consistently suppressed in liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but whether loss of individual enzymes contributes to disease progression remains unknown. We investigated the role of urea cycle enzyme argininosuccinate synthase 1 (ASS1) in diet- and carcinogen-induced liver disease using hepatocyte-specific deletion of Ass1 in mice. Complete loss of hepatic Ass1 is lethal, but a high-fat diet extends lifespan. Unexpectedly, animals with approximately 85% loss of hepatic Ass1 are markedly protected from diet-induced obesity, liver steatosis, fibrosis, and HCC. Hyperammonemia induced by hepatic Ass1 loss activates brown adipose tissue fatty acid oxidation, driving thermogenesis and increasing energy expenditure. Importantly, targeting Ass1 after obesity onset promotes weight loss and reverses liver steatosis. These findings implicate hepatic ASS1 as a critical regulator of systemic lipid metabolism with therapeutic potential against obesity, liver disease, and HCC.

article.title: Limb-localized induction of regeneration reshapes brain and amputation-site transcriptional states in adult Xenopus laevis
article.authors: Russell, S.; Miller, K.; Kaplan, D.; Levin, M.; Murugan, N. J.
article.abstract: Limb regeneration requires coordinated tissue reconstruction and nervous system reintegration, yet whether regenerative induction alters brain responses to limb loss remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomics from the paired brains and amputation sites of adult Xenopus laevis after hindlimb amputation with or without a 24 hour exposure to localized, pro-regenerative multi-drug treatment (MDT) delivered through a wearable bioreactor device. At 24 hours post treatment (24 HPT), MDT brains showed increased vascular and basement membrane transcripts and enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation and mTORC1 programs. In the limb, an exploratory integrated stress response (ISR) score increased at 11 and 24 HPT and returned to control levels by 7 days post-treatment (7 DPT), coinciding with induction of growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15), a cytokine responsive to mitochondrial stress. We detected no corresponding increase in brain ISR score. At 7 DPT, MDT brains showed enrichment of immune, heme metabolism and biosynthetic programs, reduced synaptic transmission gene expression, and increased gdf15.L. Relative to an external uninjured reference, MDT and amputation only brains showed concordant changes, with treatment modifying selected programs. Cross-species comparative analyses identified partial overlap with an axolotl regenerative glutamatergic signature and separation from selected mammalian injury profiles. These findings reveal cross-tissue responses to regenerative induction and identify candidate mechanisms of brain body communication in biomedically engineered vertebrate limb regeneration.

article.title: Structure constrained spin responses of an FMN superoxide radical-pair model in mitochondrial complex I
article.authors: Sung, J.-Y.; Antill, L. M.; Cheong, J.-H.
article.abstract: Mitochondrial complex I produces reactive oxygen species at its flavin mononucleotide (FMN) cofactor. We combined steric sampling of oxygen positions in human complex I with radical-pair spin simulations to examine how the FMN pocket shapes reaction-yield sensitivity, which provided singlet yields across FMN O2 centroid separations, magnetic fields and spin-dephasing conditions. A composite score combining geometric accessibility with normalised field and dephasing responses peaked near 3.3 in the reference 2.5 ~9.0 calculation. The highest-scoring 10% of accessible configurations had a mean separation of 3.28 (2.5th~97.5th percentiles, 2.77~3.64 ). The near contact score maximum persisted when the structural input, sampled distance range and recombination/dephasing rates were varied. At longer separations, the raw field response approached a broad plateau, while the composite score retained a near-contact maximum. Prescribed fluctuations in separation produced the greatest variability in calculated singlet yield within or close to this region. The analysis locates an FMN-centred range of accessible geometries where structural and spin-response effects combine in a model of radical-pair reaction branching.

article.title: Transcriptomic rejuvenation during intestinal and liver regeneration in mice
article.authors: Iqbal, S.; Gladyshev, V. N.
article.abstract: Aging and regeneration are fundamental biological processes, but the relationship between them is poorly understood. During intestinal regeneration, adult epithelial cells reactivate developmental programs that support repair. To investigate if this plasticity alters tissue biological age, we developed and validated intestinal tissue and epithelium-specific transcriptomic aging clocks. Across various regeneration models, epithelial states were predicted by these clocks to be younger than controls. Their expression changes were also negatively associated with intestinal stem-cell and progenitor aging signatures. The resulting younger state was characterized by YAP-associated regeneration and reduced mature enterocyte identity. In a separate irradiation model, the predicted epithelial age first increased, then fell at the peak of regeneration and later increased again during recovery. In a chemotherapy-induced injury model, epithelium in both young and old animals also reversibly transitioned through this younger state, returning to its preinjury state during recovery, although regenerative and fetal-like gene expression differed with host age. Further spatial transcriptomic analyses linked lower epithelial age with regeneration in selected injured and tumor-associated regions. In addition, liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in old animals was also accompanied by decreased transcriptomic age, which persisted to the last sampled time point, and by pathway changes negatively associated with aging signatures. Overall, these findings suggest that mammalian regeneration is associated with a transient reduction in transcriptomic age, whose timing and persistence depend on tissue and the course of repair.

article.title: Polyglutamine aggregation in the C. elegans nervous system is driven by stochastic nucleation events
article.authors: van Schijndel, V.; Tiggelaar, J.; Franken, M. S. E.; Remkes, D.; Joshi, M.; Sandhu, D.; Baars, K.; de Graaf, J. D. F.; Sinnige, T.
article.abstract: Fibrillar protein aggregation is the hallmark of a wide variety of neurodegenerative diseases. It is still poorly understood how soluble proteins transition to fibrillar aggregates, in particular within the complex environment of cells and tissues. Here, we employ the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of polyglutamine aggregation in the nervous system of a multicellular animal. By using fluorescence microscopy in combination with mathematical modelling, we find that polyglutamine aggregation occurs by stochastic nucleation in individual neurons, at a rate that is of the same order of magnitude as previously determined for muscle cells. The J-protein DNAJB6 strongly suppresses polyglutamine aggregation in both tissues, consistent with a mechanism in which aggregation is limited by primary nucleation. We confirm that the same mechanism holds true for a construct including the disease-relevant flanking regions of huntingtin exon 1. Altogether, our data reveal that polyglutamine aggregation occurs spontaneously and largely independently of the cellular context, rather than as a consequence of ageing and the associated decline in protein homeostasis.

article.title: Harnessing variation in Drosophila melanogaster reveals different routes to increased infection susceptibility over age and sex-dependent association with lifespan
article.authors: Monteiro-Black, B.; Corbally, M.-K.; Aleksandrowicz, J.; Taggart, A. M.; Langella, F.; Belmonte, R. L.; Mika, P.; Duneau, D.; Regan, J. C.
article.abstract: It is widely accepted that susceptibility to infection increases with age, usually attributed to immune system dysregulation. However, factors beyond decreased resistance mechanisms may increase susceptibility, such as changes to physiological or metabolic processes determining overall tolerance, and this may differ between individuals. We hypothesised that age-related increases in susceptibility reflect changes in both immune system function and disease tolerance, with their relative importance varying by population and sex. We assessed age-related susceptibility to bacterial pathogens in an outbred D. melanogaster population and 22 isolines. We leveraged this variation to investigate age-related infection susceptibility and lifespan, and to estimate frequencies of declines in resistance or tolerance mechanisms. Susceptibility increased early in life, and was widespread across infections and populations. Despite strong correlation between the sexes in baseline susceptibility and its decrease over age, susceptibility at old age did not correlate. Increased susceptibility was associated with impaired resistance (bona fide immunosenescence), but more frequently with reduced tolerance, which could be detected early in life, and remained low. We find susceptibility at old age predicts lifespan in males only. In conclusion, increased infection susceptibility is an early-arising ageing phenotype occurring in both sexes and driving male mortality. Infection susceptibility followed a power-law (Weibull) rather than the exponential (Gompertz) pattern typical of mortality, with each doubling of age approximately doubling susceptibility. We argue that the term 'immunosenescence' should be limited to dysregulation of resistance mechanisms, and consideration of population variation, sex, and ageing of non-immune functions is critical to fully understand age-related loss of pathogen control.

article.title: Creatine phosphagen system regulates energy metabolism and growth of trophoblasts
article.authors: Sah, N.; Zheng, C.; Stein, F. H.; Shaik, W.; Nassoura, M. B.; Mole, L. M.; Rajupalem, R.; Pizzo, D.; Meads, M.; Soncin, F.
article.abstract: The creatine (Cr)-creatine kinase (CK)-phosphocreatine (PCr) system maintains ATP homeostasis in tissues with high energy demands, but its role in early human placental development remains poorly understood. We characterized Cr-CK-PCr system components across gestation and investigated its function in trophoblast development. Proteins involved in Cr biosynthesis, transport, and utilization were examined in first-trimester, second-trimester, and term human placentae (n=3-6/group). Components showed gestational age- and compartment-specific localization. The biosynthetic enzymes AGAT and GAMT localized predominantly to fetal villous mesenchyme and broadly across villous compartments, respectively. CKB was enriched in fetal mesenchyme, whereas CKMT1 was broadly expressed across trophoblast subtypes. The main Cr transporter SLC6A8 was abundant in syncytiotrophoblast early in gestation but shifted predominantly to fetal blood vessels at term. To determine functional importance, primary human trophoblast stem cells (hTSCs) were treated with a creatine analog, cyclocreatine (cCr; 0-40 mM), for 48 h. Treatment with 20 mM cCr reduced proliferation (P<0.001), decreased EGFR expression (P<0.05), induced cell-cycle arrest (P<0.0001), and increased apoptosis (P<0.0001). cCr also impaired mitochondrial and glycolytic function (P<0.01) with morphological evidence of mitochondrial stress. Consistently, treatment of primary human trophoblast organoids with cCr reduced organoid growth and EGFR expression (P<0.05). Together, these findings demonstrate that the Cr-CK-PCr system is dynamically expressed across human placental development and that disruption of Cr/PCr metabolism compromises trophoblast bioenergetics, proliferation, and survival, supporting its importance in placental development and providing a foundation for investigating its contribution to pregnancy disorders associated with altered placental energy metabolism.

article.title: Transgenerational pathogen defence extends beyond behavioural avoidance
article.authors: Zwoinska, M. K.; Widjaja, A. N.; Akgül, A. D.; Altan, A. S.; Aydın, D.; Cukurbaglı, D.; Duxbury, E. M.; Harris, I.; Maklakov, A. A.; Renhuldt, N. T.; Venkataramani, A. G.; Lind, M. I.; Chen, H.-y.
article.abstract: Transgenerational plasticity can prepare descendants for environmental stress, but its generality and adaptive value remain unclear. Here we tested for adaptive transgenerational effects of exposure to the bacterial pathogen Pseudomonas vranovensis across five Caenorhabditis species. Pathogen exposure reduced rate-sensitive fitness in all five species, but behavioural responses varied across species and generations. In C. elegans, exposed parents and their F2 descendants showed increased pathogen avoidance. In C. remanei, pathogen exposure increased attraction in females, whereas their F2 female descendants showed greater avoidance. We found no F2 behavioural response in C. kamaaina, C. tropicalis or C. briggsae. Remarkably, however, ancestral exposure increased F2 larval survival on the pathogen in C. elegans, C. remanei and C. tropicalis. In C. tropicalis this survival benefit occurred without behavioural avoidance. The two species showing transgenerational avoidance had the closest sequence matches between the bacterial small RNA Pv1 and its candidate neuronal target maco-1, suggesting a possible molecular basis for variation in the response. Our results show that shared susceptibility to a pathogen does not imply similarity in transgenerational response, and that ancestral exposure can benefit descendants without inheritance of pathogen avoidance.

article.title: Ribosome-Associated GTPase Drg1 Links Cytosolic Translation to Mitochondrial Homeostasis
article.authors: Saha, S.; Bhattacharya, A.; Jin, H.
article.abstract: Coordination of the functionalities among key organelles is essential for maintaining the complexity and adaptability of the eukaryotic cell. Functionally versatile proteins, such as GTPases, often assume important roles in this process. A ribosome-binding GTPase called Developmentally-regulated GTP-binding (Drg) protein is a conserved family of GTPases that promotes protein synthesis and regulates cytoskeletal dynamics, suggesting their importance for cell growth and proliferation. Mitochondrial proteostasis requires coordination between cytosolic translation and the targeting, import, and assembly of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins. However, the ribosome-associated factors that support this coordination remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify the conserved GTPase Drg1, one of the two Drg paralogues in eukaryotic cells, as a translation factor required for mitochondrial homeostasis and cellular fitness. Human Drg1 and its cofactor Dfrp1 are associated with translating ribosomes and co-sedimented with polysomes. Deletion of Drg1 in HEK293T cells caused altered mitochondrial architecture, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP production, and impaired expression of a mitochondrially targeted reporter. Re-expression of wild-type Drg1 restored ATP production and reporter expression, whereas a GTPase-deficient Drg1 mutant failed to provide comparable rescue in ATP production, demonstrating that Drg1 catalytic activity is required for its cellular function. Mitochondria-directed APEX2 proximity proteomics further connected Drg1-dependent translation to proteins involved in mitochondrial protein import, respiratory-chain function, and mitochondrial protein synthesis. Reporter analyses indicated that Drg1 loss preferentially compromises productive translation toward the 3' region of the coding sequence. Together, these findings establish Drg1 as a ribosome-associated translation factor that supports the synthesis and homeostasis of proteins required for mitochondrial function. At the molecular level, loss of cellular homeostasis that is caused by compromised translation of cytoplasmically synthesized proteins functionally related to mitochondria underpins the observed phenomenon. Our results reveal a previously underappreciated connection between the cytosolic translation machinery and mitochondrial maintenance and provide a framework for understanding how defects in a conserved translational GTPase impair cellular energy metabolism and physiology.

article.title: A high-throughput nanoscale imaging platform for direct visualization and rapid measurement of telomeres at single-molecule resolution
article.authors: Collen Jackson-Cook; Lilia Gheghiani; Andrey Mikheykin; Dylan Van Laeken; Daniel Guest; Kellie Archer; Harold Riethman; Jason Reed
article.abstract: Abstract Telomere length is a biomarker of aging, cancer and telomeropathies, with some of the strongest health-related associations occurring at the extremes of the telomere-length spectrum. Critically short telomeres can drive chromosome instability, cellular stress and senescence, yet conventional assays largely provide population-average measurements that obscure these biologically important molecules, and the underlying heterogeneity of individual chromosome ends. In addition, amplification bias associated with highly repetitive telomeric sequences and inter-laboratory variability can limit measurement reproducibility. Although emerging technologies provide higher-resolution analyses, they often require high DNA input, specialized sample preparation, or complex instrumentation and bioinformatic tools, restricting broader adoption. Here, we present a high-throughput single-molecule platform that overcomes these barriers through an automated, user-friendly nanoscale imaging workflow compatible with standard genomic DNA preparations. The method combines a unique dual CRISPR-Cas9 telomere boundary labeling strategy with amplification-free magnetic-bead-based enrichment, preserving the native telomere-length distribution while minimizing representation bias. Using only 500 ng of input DNA and 2–4 h of hands-on processing, the assay accurately resolves intact telomeres spanning ~50 bp to >50 kb within the same sample, enabling simultaneous characterization of the full telomere-length spectrum. It also demonstrates high reproducibility across technical replicates and independent operators (ICC up to 0.90). Validation in telomere-length models, replicative aging systems, and clinical biospecimens, together with subtelomeric barcoding for chromosome-arm assignment, establishes a scalable platform for chromosome-resolved telomere profiling, biomarker development, and future clinical implementation in aging, cancer, and telomere biology.
